root_idea.summary: The root centers on preparing to watch or intercept something along its route, and extends to watching, guarding, a station of observation, and things prepared to lie in wait.
root_idea.development: From watchful readiness, the lexicon develops meanings of setting something in readiness or in another's path, watching or guarding, places and agents of surveillance, and specialized terms for ambushes, predators, rain, and herbage.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested verbal noun, normalized as the Form IV citation noun إِرْصَاد.
Distinct Quran-attested place noun مِرْصَاد, conventionally specialized for watchfulness.
Distinct Quran-attested noun/adjectival form رَصَد denoting a watcher or guard.

senses.definition: Preparing or setting up a station for watchful opposition or surveillance.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the verbal noun denotes establishing something as a place or means of watchful readiness, rather than generic preparation alone.

senses.definition: A place, position, or route where one watches or lies in wait; an ambush post.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction can refer to every route or way used as a position for watching or interception.

senses.definition: A station or position specially designated for watching or lying in wait.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran it is applied figuratively to Hell as a station lying in wait for those who pass through, and to the Lord's watchful position from which no person's deeds escape.

senses.definition: A watcher or guard, whether an individual or a group, stationed to observe, protect, or lie in wait.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic contexts use the form for guards or watchers, including those stationed before and behind a bearer of revelation; the form may function as a noun or an adjectival description.

senses.definition: A person or thing kept under watch; a watched or guarded party.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran-focused lexical discussion allows رَصَد to refer to the watched party or object, singular or plural, as well as to the watcher; the supplied Quranic contexts are commonly understood as referring to guards.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To watch, wait for, or lie in wait for someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe waiting on a road, watching for a thing, or awaiting an opportunity to spring; the object may be construed with لَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small quantity or early fall of rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported applications vary: it may be the first rain, rain following or awaited after other rain, or a shower falling at once; رَصْدَةٌ is also reported as a name for such rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small quantity of herbage in land awaiting the season's rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized agricultural use associated with land in which seasonal rain is hoped for.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To charge someone with watching or guarding a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction takes the person charged with surveillance and the thing to be watched or guarded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prepare or make ready a person or thing for someone; to set it in his way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The prepared object may be an army, a mount, property, money, punishment, good, or evil; these examples illustrate the construction rather than an object-class restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To requite or recompense someone with good or evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an extended application of preparing something for a person as a consequence awaiting him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To show, cast up, or produce a reckoning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported extended or technical usage concerning the presentation of an account or calculation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A watching or waiting; in an idiom, an act of watching for good or evil understood as requital.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom presents repeated or individual watchings as consequences that will not miss the person concerned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pitfall or pit prepared for a lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized hunting term, synonymous with زُبْيَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A brass or silver ring in the straps or cords by which a sword is suspended.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical object-term distinct from the ambush meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who lies in wait for people on a road in order to take their property unjustly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term denotes a person characterized by predatory roadside ambush.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that waits until other camels have drunk and then drinks herself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is a conventional animal description of delayed drinking behavior.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beast of prey, wolf, or serpent that lies in wait to spring or bite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is applied to predatory creatures waiting for an opportunity to attack, including a serpent waiting for passers-by.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Snares or traps prepared for catching beasts of prey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This plural denotes prepared catching devices and is synonymous with وَصَائِد in the cited usage.
This is a conventional designation derived from the lion's watchful or waiting posture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who watches or waits, especially one awaiting an opportunity to requite beneficence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explicitly related to رَاصِد and is used in a construction where waiting culminates in recompense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land rained upon by a rain termed رَصْد or رَصْدَة, or land expected to produce herbage after such rain; also land containing a small amount of that herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is used of land whose rainfall or incipient herbage gives hope of further growth; variant forms are reported in the lexical discussion.

cautions: رَصَد is Quranically tagged as both noun and adjective. The Quran-focused lexical discussion permits it to denote either watcher(s) or the watched or guarded party, although the supplied contextual readings favor the watcher/guard sense.
